rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance - Annual Rent Increase Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords in rent-controlled buildings cannot raise rent more than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index, capped at 4% per year, and only if the building is registered and in substantial compliance with housing codes.
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings as defined in the ordinance are subject to rent control.
rules.exemptions: Allowable annual increase not permitted if dwelling is not in substantial compliance or landlord has not met registration requirements.
rules.penalty: No rent increase shall be approved for any landlord who has failed to comply with all provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, including registration.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is in substantial compliance with housing codes and registration requirements
